root_cause.text: ext4_mb_release() conditionally flushed the discard workqueue only when the current mount option DISCARD was set, but pending discard work could have been queued earlier under a different mount state, leaving it unfinished upon unmount and potentially causing use-after-free or resource leaks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD))` guard around `flush_work(&sbi->s_discard_work)` and `WARN_ON_ONCE(!list_empty(&sbi->s_discard_list))`, making these operations unconditional. The commit description explicitly states the problem: "If the filesystem is initially mounted with the discard option, deleting files will populate sbi->s_discard_list and queue s_discard_work. If it is then remounted with nodiscard, the EXT4_MOUNT_DISCARD flag is cleared, but the pending s_discard_work is neither cancelled nor flushed."

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure discard work is always flushed and integrity checked during filesystem release, even when not mounted with the DISCARD option.
intent_record.what: Removed the `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD))` conditional around the flush_work and WARN_ON_ONCE calls in ext4_mb_release, so that these operations are now executed unconditionally.
intent_record.how: Previously, the discard work was flushed and the discard list check was only performed when the DISCARD mount option was enabled. Now these operations occur every time the filesystem is released, regardless of the mount option.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by ensuring discard work is always flushed during filesystem release regardless of the DISCARD mount option, which matches the root cause of conditional flushing leading to potential use-after-free or resource leaks.

candidates.rationale: This conditional statement gates the entire discard work flush and integrity check, causing them to be skipped if the current mount option does not include DISCARD, even though pending discard work may have been queued when the option was previously set.

This flush operation is the critical cleanup action that ensures pending discard work is completed; it is only executed inside the conditional block, leaving work unfinished if the DISCARD option is not currently set.
